candidates.title: Two invitations
candidates.body:
He held out a twig. I took it to stop him holding it out.

Another bird offered me ice.

I wanted the ice. Had to put the twig down.

He picked it up. Held it out again.
candidates.visibleScene: Three common ravens stand together on snow. The upper-left bird holds a pale curved twig/root-like object over the central-right bird. The lower bird turns upward toward the central bird. Black feather detail and the held object are clear; no ice piece is clearly isolated in the lower bird bill at this instant.
candidates.fictionBoundary: The observer reports repeated twig offering to the central raven and ice offered by the lower raven. Maud is the central recipient. Accepting the twig, putting it down, preference for ice, the other bird retrieving it and her motive are fictional sequence. Do not describe the whole sequence as recorded. Object is called a twig after the observer stick identification; no plant species inferred. Companion sex is fictional and no mating or lifetime bond is added.
candidates.canon: Retain adult female Maud Overhead, Corvus corax, Yellowstone forest and rock country44.7,-110.5 and existing avatar. Source Mayo, Yukon is provenance; snow and conifers suit the fictional home without moving her. Append independent adult winter social scene. All four admitted passages preserved; Maud155 hanging remains held for image quality. No gift-offering scene currently admitted.
candidates.payoff: Accepting an unwanted offering briefly ends the gesture; making room for the preferred object gives the first bird another chance. Particular social persistence, no communal meal, food retrieval or audience embarrassment.
candidates.reviewFlag: The second object is primarily observer-attested, not visually distinct in this still. The photograph does clearly establish the three-party interaction and raised first offering. Lead should assess this boundary without requiring every temporal action in one frame.

holds.title: The tree’s turn
holds.body:
I went up to see the willow bend. It bent.

Lay across it to make it bend farther.

Now my feet are on different branches. Every time I move one, something else lifts.

I'm going to let the tree finish first.
holds.reason: HOLD prose: sharp young raccoon draped over branches, but the invented seesaw problem and late quip do not earn an episode; repeats balance material. No childhood canon addition.

holds.title: Still on the tree
holds.body:
Pulled the twig toward me. It came. Let go and it went back.

Did it again.

Held it for longer this time, until my neck began to ache. The tree was still willing to wait.
holds.reason: HOLD prose: fixed-branch beak contact supports tugging, but elastic return is not distinctive enough and the closing anthropomorphism is a stock quip.
